short: The lead ship of the Royal Navy's modern aircraft carriers, restoring British global strike capabilities.
full:
Commissioned on 7 December 2017, HMS Queen Elizabeth (R08) is the lead ship of her class and the largest warship ever built for the Royal Navy. Unlike American carriers, it utilises a short take-off and vertical landing (STOVL) configuration, operating a bespoke air group built around the advanced F-35B Lightning II stealth fighter. Its design features a unique twin-island superstructure to separate ship navigation and flight control operations.

The entry of the Queen Elizabeth class into service marked a major resurgence in British maritime power projection, replacing expeditionary capabilities lost when the Invincible class was retired. It serves as the centrepiece of UK carrier strike groups, capable of deploying worldwide in conjunction with allied navies. Alongside its sister ship, HMS Prince of Wales, it ensures Britain retains a leading role in global naval operations for decades to come.
